title: A denominator at one vertex extends to a denominator morphism of distinguished triangles
statement: Let $S$ be a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure of a triangulated category [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], and let $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ be a distinguished triangle in the pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every morphism $s:X'\to X$ in $S$, there exist a distinguished triangle $(X',Y',Z',f',g',h')$ and morphisms $s':Y'\to Y$ and $s'':Z'\to Z$ in $S$ such that $(s,s',s'')$ is a morphism of distinguished triangles to $(X,Y,Z)$. The analogous assertion holds with $Y$ or $Z$ in place of $X$ (after rotating the triangles).

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), construction of objects over a prescribed denominator

proof.text: For the prescribed denominator s:X'\to X, form the composite f\circ s:X'\to Y. By (TR1) in [def-weil-triangulated-category], it is the first map of a distinguished cone triangle X'\xrightarrow{f\circ s}Y\xrightarrow{g'}Z'\xrightarrow{h'}X'[1].

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), construction over a prescribed denominator; TR1 cone triangle

proof.text: The square with components s:X′→X and id_Y:Y→Y commutes. MS1 puts id_Y in S. Apply MS6 in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] directly to the two distinguished triangles and this square: it chooses a third component t:Z′→Z in S satisfying both remaining triangle-morphism squares. Thus (s,id_Y,t) is the required denominator morphism. This is a compatible TR3 completion, not a claim that an arbitrary TR3 completion belongs to S.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), construction over a prescribed denominator; TR3 and compatibility axiom MS6

proof.text: For a prescribed denominator s:Y′→Y, use TR1/TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] to complete s≫g as the second map of a distinguished triangle with third vertex Z. Rotate both triangles and apply MS6 with components s and id_Z. Lift the resulting third component through the full shift-by-one functor; MS5 in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] gives membership in S, and faithfulness cancels the rotation signs to recover the first square. For s:Z′→Z, complete s≫h as the third map of a distinguished triangle with first vertex X. Inverse-rotate both triangles and apply MS6 with components s[-1] and id_X, using MS5 for s[-1]. Cancel the shift counit isomorphism in the last resulting square to recover the original second square. Triangle.homMk supplies both morphisms with the prescribed component exactly s.

lean.statement: theorem denominator_triangle_completion {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] (S : MorphismProperty C) (hS : S.IsSaturatedMultiplicativeSystem) [S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation] (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) : (∀ (X' : C) (s : X' ⟶ T.obj₁), S s → ∃ (Y' Z' : C) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Y' ⟶ Z') (h' : Z' ⟶ X'⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk f' g' h' ∈ distTriang C ∧ ∃ φ : Triangle.mk f' g' h' ⟶ T, φ.hom₁ = s ∧ S φ.hom₂ ∧ S φ.hom₃) ∧ (∀ (Y' : C) (s : Y' ⟶ T.obj₂), S s → ∃ (X' Z' : C) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Y' ⟶ Z') (h' : Z' ⟶ X'⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk f' g' h' ∈ distTriang C ∧ ∃ φ : Triangle.mk f' g' h' ⟶ T, φ.hom₂ = s ∧ S φ.hom₁ ∧ S φ.hom₃) ∧ (∀ (Z' : C) (s : Z' ⟶ T.obj₃), S s → ∃ (X' Y' : C) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Y' ⟶ Z') (h' : Z' ⟶ X'⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk f' g' h' ∈ distTriang C ∧ ∃ φ : Triangle.mk f' g' h' ⟶ T, φ.hom₃ = s ∧ S φ.hom₁ ∧ S φ.hom₂)
